identity.title: Substructures in the Keplerian disc around the O-type (proto-)star G17.64+0.16

paper_type_evidence.quote: In this letter we report on the observations of G17.64 using the ALMA long-baselines at Band 6.

evidence.quote: Located at 2.2 kpc and with a bolometric luminosity of 1$\times$10$^5$ L$_{\odot}$[^3] (cite: Lumsden2013)

question.value: Does the disc around the O-type (proto)star G17.64+0.16 show substructure, Keplerian rotation, and gravitational stability when resolved at ~20 mas (~40 au)?

evidence.quote: we now fully resolve the dust and molecular line emission and for the first time uncover clear enhanced substructures in the disc around this massive forming O-star.
project ID: 2017.1.00098.S - PI: Maud
observations of G17.64 using the ALMA long-baselines at Band 6
all four spectral-windows (SPWs) were configured with the widest bandwidth of 1.875 GHz
We detected SiO (5$-$4) and the H30$\alpha$ radio-recombination line
We detected SiO (5$-$4) and the H30$\alpha$ radio-recombination line
in configuration C43-10, with 43 antennas

angular_resolution.value: 20x15 mas (44x33 au), PA -88.4 deg, continuum robust 0.0

analysis_steps.goal: Image continuum and measure disc size, inclination

method.value: Fit ellipse to the 50 sigma contour; inclination from axis ratio assuming a circular thin disc

evidence.quote: Fitting an ellipse to the 50$\sigma$ contour level ($\sim$2.0 mJy beam$^{-1}$) we find that the disc measures 93$\times$71 mas.

assumptions.value: Circular thin disc with settled mm grains

evidence.quote: Assuming a circular thin-disc where the mm-sized dust grains have settled to the mid-plane

validation.value: Uncertainty from fitting at 30 and 70 sigma contours

evidence.quote: The uncertainty propagates from fitting the disc size at the 30$\sigma$ and 70$\sigma$ contours

analysis_steps.goal: Subtract free-free point source and estimate disc mass

method.value: Point-source subtraction in visibilities at the upper-limit free-free flux; optically thin mass with Hildebrand formula, Td = 50, 100, 150 K

evidence.quote: resulting lower limit optically thin disc mass ranges from 0.6 to 2.6 M$_{\odot}$ following (cite: Hildebrand1983)

assumptions.value: gas-to-dust 100, kappa=1.0 cm2/g at 1.3 mm, Td 50-150 K, d=2.2 kpc

evidence.quote: g is the gas-to-dust ratio = 100

validation.value: Imaging done with and without phase-centre shift to rule out sidelobe artefacts

evidence.quote: no notable differences were seen in any of our images.

analysis_steps.goal: H2O moment maps and PV diagram

method.value: Moment 0/1 maps; PV cut at PA 25.9 deg, 5 pixel width, PA from Gaussian centres of blue and red moment-0 maps

evidence.quote: The cut for the PV diagram was taken at a position angle of 25.9$^{\circ}$ using a width of 5 pixels

method.value: Disc-only Keplerian PV model matched by eye to contours, outer radius 120 au, inclination 40 deg, inner radius 25-30 au

evidence.quote: fix the disc outer radius to 120 au as per the dust and H$_2$O maps and also revise the inclination angle to 40$\pm$5$^{\circ}$
fitting is made by-eye matching equivalent contour levels

method.value: Q = c_s kappa/(pi G Sigma); Sigma from column density times mu m_H, mu=2.3; T(R) propto R^-0.4 anchored to a 45 Msun O star

evidence.quote: The temperature of the disc is calculated using $T(R)\propto (R/R_0)^{-0.4}$ (cite: Whitney2003)

assumptions.value: Optically thin; steeper T profile or optical depth would lower Q

evidence.quote: If we use a steeper temperature profile (cite: Brinch2010) the temperature in the disc is below 150 K

validation.value: Computed for minimal and maximal free-free removal

evidence.quote: Toomre Q maps for G17.64 where the minimal and maximal free-free contamination is removed
Data calibration used the casa pipeline, version 5.1.1
This paper makes use of the least-squares fitting by (cite: HammelLS).
The peak flux is 25.12 mJy beam$^{-1}$
We recover an integrated flux of 79.14 mJy (within a 60 mas radius circle)
we estimate the disc inclination as $\sim$40$\pm$4$^{\circ}$
resulting lower limit optically thin disc mass ranges from 0.6 to 2.6 M$_{\odot}$
the modelled central mass must be increased to 45$\pm$10 M$_{\odot}$
has the lowest Toomre Q values, between 2 and 4

findings_qualitative.value: Dust disc shows a ring-like enhancement at 65-97 au, possibly an underlying spiral

evidence.quote: the continuum emission has a significant enhancement of dust emission in a ring-like, or possibly underlying spiral structure

claims.hypothesis: Does the disc around G17.64 have substructure?
claims.experiment: Band 6 long-baseline continuum imaging at 20 mas
claims.result: Ring-like enhancement at 65-97 au; arcs peak at 3-4 mJy/beam
claims.finding: First substructure seen in a disc around an O-type protostar

evidence.quote: G17.64 is the first massive O-type source in which substructure has been observed in the disc.

claims.hypothesis: Is the H2O emission tracing a Keplerian disc and what is the central mass?
claims.experiment: PV diagram and by-eye disc model
claims.finding: Keplerian rotation about a ~45 Msun star

evidence.quote: we confirm Keplerian rotation about a central mass of 45$\pm$10 M$_{\odot}$

claims.result: Q 2-4 in the ring for T>150 K
claims.finding: Locally stable in the optically thin, hot case

evidence.quote: The disc is found to be locally stable through a Toomre Q analysis in the optically thin case when disc temperature are $>$150 K.

why_this_method.value: Extreme excitation H2O line chosen to trace the inner disc

evidence.quote: The extreme excitation energy of this line makes it particularly suited for tracing very inner regions of a molecular disc

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Binary companion or earlier spiral instabilities considered as causes of the ring

evidence.quote: it is plausible that a binary companion is the cause of the ring-like enhancements

limitations_admitted.value: Free-free contamination is uncertain so the inner ring is speculative

evidence.quote: Although speculative, because the free-free contamination is uncertain, we tentatively reveal an enhanced inner ring

referee_caveats_inferred: Stellar mass fit is by eye with no formal uncertainty or degeneracy exploration
Single-band continuum cannot separate optical depth and temperature effects
Substructure could be partly imaging or self-calibration artefacts at a dynamic range of 640
